title: The growth-needs clinic
subtitle: Summer 1 • Judge growth with more than height
objective: Identify requirements for healthy plant growth and use height plus leaf evidence to evaluate a care claim.

sow.exactOutcome: Identify what plants need to grow well (light, water, warmth, nutrients).
sow.alignment: Chronological continuation of the supplied SOW. This lesson develops or reviews the named outcome; it does not claim an accreditation award.

priorLearning: Roots absorb water and mineral nutrients.
Green leaves make sugars using light.
success: Name light, water, suitable warmth and minerals.
Include air and sufficient space in a care plan.
Use leaf condition as well as height.

vocabulary.meaning: Something needed for a process or life.
A substance needed for healthy growth.
Information used to judge a claim.

equipment: Printed shared evidence and one chosen pupil route; pencil; optional ruler; projector or offline HTML.
preparation: Print the shared evidence, one response route and exit page. Routes are alternatives, not a workload ladder.
Read the worked answers. Prepare an oral, pointing or adult-scribed route where useful.
safety: This is a paper evidence clinic; no plants are deliberately deprived or overheated.
For optional care observation, use adult-selected non-toxic plants, no tasting, and wash hands afterwards.
practicalAlternative: All core reasoning uses the supplied evidence and can be completed in 40 minutes without a live practical.

misconceptions.claim: The tallest seedling must be healthiest.
misconceptions.correction: A dark-grown seedling can elongate and become pale; height alone is insufficient.
misconceptions.check: Compare groups A and B using leaf condition.

misconceptions.claim: More water and warmth always help.
misconceptions.correction: Too much water or unsuitable heat can harm growth; suitable amounts depend on the plant.
misconceptions.check: Ask for appropriate, not maximum, provision.

misconceptions.claim: Every seed needs exactly the same light to germinate.
misconceptions.correction: Species differ; many use stored reserves before green growth is established.
misconceptions.check: Distinguish germination from sustained green growth.

access.supported: Short choices, word bank and pointing or adult-scribed reasons; same core scientific goal.
access.standard: Make a short evidence-based explanation or record using the supplied information.
access.stretch: Apply the core idea to a changed case, evaluate evidence or identify a limit.
access.regulation: Preview the sequence. Offer seated observation, quiet paired rehearsal, private feedback and a pass from public sharing. Routes respond to current access needs, not a diagnosis.

sources.title: Department for Education: science programmes of study

sources.title: Science and Plants for Schools: plant biology animations
sources.note: Checked 8 September 2026. Scientific background for our original simplified diagrams: photosynthesis, growth and transport. No external animation is required or embedded.

sources.title: Royal Horticultural Society: sowing seeds indoors
sources.note: Checked 8 September 2026. Germination uses stored reserves and requires appropriate water, oxygen and temperature; seedling care differs from starting germination.

slides.title: Which plant needs a better care plan?
slides.notes: Introduce constructed records of matched young bean seedlings. Do not present this as the class’s actual experiment.

slides.title: Retrieve the inputs
body: 2. What do green leaves need to make sugars?
3. Are minerals the same as ready-made sugar?
slides.notes: 1 roots. 2 light, water and carbon dioxide from air; light enough for the short prompt. 3 no.

slides.title: I check the whole set of needs
body: Use suitable warmth, air and space.
slides.notes: Think aloud: “Providing water does not make light unnecessary. I check each requirement. I ask what is suitable for this plant, rather than assuming more is always better.”

visual.title: Requirements work together
visual.description: A growing green plant receives light energy, water and mineral nutrients, and exchanges gases with air. Appropriate temperature and space also matter. Amounts vary by species and conditions.

elements.text: More is not always better. Requirements vary.

slides.title: I refuse to use height alone
slides.notes: Shares I do time. Think aloud: “13 is greater than 8, but pale small leaves change my judgement. Dark-grown seedlings can become elongated; taller is not a general health score.” The examples show selected seedlings from the constructed groups.

visual.title: Taller does not automatically mean healthier
visual.description: Constructed day-7 examples: light-grown group A has an 8 cm green seedling; dark-grown group B has a 13 cm pale elongated seedling. Heights alone cannot indicate healthy sustained growth.

elements.text:
A: light available
8 cm; green leaves
Record height AND leaf condition before judging growth.

slides.title: I separate seed and green-plant stages
slides.notes: Shares I do time. Think aloud: “A seed starting in darkness does not prove that an established green plant can grow well indefinitely without light.” Seeds also differ in light requirements.

visual.title: Starting from a seed is a different stage
visual.description: A germinating seed can use stored food reserves. An established green plant needs light for sustained photosynthesis. Species differ in whether seeds need light to germinate.

elements.text:
Uses stored reserves.
Needs water, oxygen and
suitable temperature.
Some seeds also need light to germinate; check the species.

slides.title: The evidence clinic: compare A and B
body: Make a care judgement with a reason.
slides.notes: W1: B is taller but pale; A shows stronger evidence of healthy growth here. All seedlings started about 3 cm. Two plants per group are supplied; not enough for a universal conclusion.

table.caption: Constructed sample data: two seedlings per group; all started about 3 cm

slides.title: Choose a repair that fits the condition
slides.notes: W2: C adjust watering appropriately; D provide suitable warmth. Do not tell pupils to flood a pot or put a plant on a radiator. The cases stipulate the changed condition, not a general diagnosis from drooping alone.
slides.reveal: Address the stated missing requirement; keep other needs suitable.

slides.title: B is 13 cm and pale. A is 8 cm and green.
slides.notes: Correct second option. Return to leaf condition if height alone dominates.

options.text: B must be healthier because it is taller.
options.feedback: Pale small leaves challenge that conclusion.

options.text: Height alone cannot establish which grows well.
options.feedback: Leaf condition and suitable inputs also matter.

slides.title: Choose your science route
slides.notes: Set ONE route. Use the shared constructed table. Do not diagnose an actual plant from one symptom. Accept suitable care language and more than one observation; do not reward a universal care recipe.

slides.title: Make your own evidence record
slides.notes: Use the shared constructed table. Do not diagnose an actual plant from one symptom. Accept suitable care language and more than one observation; do not reward a universal care recipe.

slides.title: Check what the evidence can show
body: Point to the clue you used.
slides.notes: Shares independent time. Ask for a reason, not just a correct word. Use the shared constructed table. Do not diagnose an actual plant from one symptom. Accept suitable care language and more than one observation; do not reward a universal care recipe.

slides.title: Lundy loop: improve the shared account
slides.notes: Listen to a selected pupil revision and visibly adopt a scientifically accurate contribution. Offer private, written or partner feedback.
slides.prompt: What changed when we added leaf evidence?
slides.reveal: A taller pale seedling does not automatically show healthier growth.

slides.title: Keep the useful change
slides.notes: Shares review time. Name how a pupil contribution changed a label, method or conclusion. Do not rank pupils.
slides.reveal: A taller pale seedling does not automatically show healthier growth.

slides.title: Three final checks
body: E2. Is height alone enough to judge healthy growth?
E3. Do mineral nutrients replace light?
slides.notes: Collect brief individual evidence. Use the answer key and re-teach the specified misconception if needed.

pupilPages.title: Shared evidence • Constructed growth clinic
pupilPages.intro: Two young bean seedlings per group; all began about 3 cm. Same species, age, pots and observation interval. Only the stated care condition changed.

blocks.text: Healthy green growth also requires air, suitable warmth, water, mineral nutrients and enough space. Amounts differ between plants. These records are supplied examples, not pupil measurements.

blocks.prompt: W1. Which group is taller, A or B? Which other clue matters?
W2. Give a suitable care change for C and for D.

pupilPages.title: Route 1 • Make the care checklist
pupilPages.intro: Word bank: light / water / suitable warmth / mineral nutrients / air / space.

blocks.prompt: S1. Name four things needed for plants to grow well.
S2. Does B’s greater height prove better health?
S3. Which leaf clue helps you judge B?
S4. In C, which stated requirement needs attention?

pupilPages.title: Route 2 • Write a care brief
pupilPages.intro: Use at least two observations when comparing growth.

blocks.prompt: M1. Compare A and B using height and leaf condition.
M2. Give a care change for C and explain why it fits this case.
M3. Explain why “the hottest place and most water” is a poor rule.
M4. Explain why mineral nutrients do not replace light.

pupilPages.title: Route 3 • Challenge the headline
pupilPages.intro: Headline: “Darkness is best for all plants because group B grew tallest.”

blocks.prompt: T1. Use two pieces of evidence to challenge the headline.
T2. Why can two seedlings per group not settle a claim about all plants?
T3. A seed germinates in darkness. Explain why this does not prove the headline.
T4. Give a better headline limited to these records.

pupilPages.title: Exit and reflection
pupilPages.intro: Point, draw, write or tell an adult.

blocks.prompt: E2. Is height alone enough to judge healthy growth?
E3. Do mineral nutrients replace light?
R1. Which idea did you improve or defend? What evidence helped?
R2. What useful question would you investigate next?

answers.label: Retrieval 1–3
answers.answer: 1 roots. 2 light, water and carbon dioxide from air. 3 no.

answers.label: We do W1–W2
answers.answer: W1 B is taller (12–13 cm versus 8–9 cm); pale small leaves matter, while A is green with several leaves. W2 adjust C’s water supply appropriately; move D to suitable warmth while preserving other needs.

answers.label: Hinge
answers.answer: Second option correct. Greater height is only one observation; green plants need light for sustained photosynthesis.

answers.label: S1–S4
answers.answer: S1 any four from light, water, suitable warmth, minerals, air and space; ensure the four named SOW requirements are taught. S2 no. S3 pale small leaves. S4 water.

answers.label: M1–M4
answers.answer: M1 B taller but pale/small leaves; A shorter and green with several leaves. M2 appropriate watering because C explicitly had too little; avoid flooding. M3 excessive heat/water can be unsuitable and species differ. M4 minerals are needed substances, whereas light supplies energy for photosynthesis.

answers.label: T1–T4
answers.answer: T1 B 12–13 cm but pale and small-leaved; A 8–9 cm and green. T2 small sample, one species, one stage and one interval cannot justify all plants. T3 stored seed reserves can support initial growth; sustained green growth needs photosynthesis, and seeds differ in light requirements. T4 e.g. in these examples, dark-grown seedlings were taller but paler; height alone did not show healthy growth.

answers.label: Exit E1–E3
answers.answer: E1 any two valid requirements. E2 no, include leaf condition and other evidence. E3 no: different requirements have different roles.

answers.label: R1–R2
answers.answer: Responses vary. Credit a scientific revision, evidence-based defence or relevant next question. A private or oral response has equal value.

teacherNotes: 40 minutes: opening 2, retrieval 3, I do 7, We do 8, hinge 3, independent 12, review 3, exit 2. Zero-minute slides share the named stage time.
BUILD uses the supplied Year 3 science anchor with age-respectful contexts for older pupils. Supported, standard and stretch are selectable routes within the pathway.

Interactive We do: predict first, test against the controlled SVG model or supplied evidence, then explain or revise. Shared W tasks offer the equivalent paper discussion. Animation is a teaching representation, not filmed experimental evidence.
Keep constructed evidence separate from actual class observations. Do not invent measurements or require internet research.
Secure core includes light, water, appropriate warmth and minerals plus awareness of air/space. A pupil should reject height-only judgement using the pale-leaf clue.

interactive.title: Growth clinic: choose the relevant evidence
